S3.Q2:
B's face band (rows 87–116) sits at a median of 33–43 against a floor of 74 — I sampled columns x=40, 150, 300 and 400 and got face/floor ratios of 0.49, 0.47, 0.51, 0.49. That constant half-value across four columns of wildly different engine brightness is the whole trick: it's an orientation relationship, not a gradient. Above it B runs a joint-free cap strip (rows 79–84, median 68–71 — essentially floor value, as a horizontal surface should be), then a 2-px near-black arris shadow at rows 85–86 (median 29) before the face drops away.
A has none of this: its lowest wall rows (111–116) measure 59–62 against the same 74 floor — ratios of 0.81 to 0.93 at those same four columns — so the base of the wall and the floor it meets are within a few values of each other and the wall dissolves into the ground plane. A's six horizontal dark lines (rows 53, 65, 69, 79, 93–96, 107) are all equal-weight mortar joints; not one of them is heavier than the others, so there is no candidate for a top edge. B has exactly one dominant horizontal residual in the whole band, at rows 85–91, and it is in the right place. A also carries a faint painted top-light on every course — each course opens bright at its top row and dims to its bottom (rows 81→92: 53→46; rows 97→106: 53→48) *against* the global gradient, which brightens downward.
flips: Reserve the bottom 32 px of A's wall (rows 85–116) as the inner face and drop it to ~0.5 of the floor's value at every column — floor median is 74, so the face should sit at 35–38 median and hold that ratio into the dark left edge (x=40: floor 51, face 25) as well as the lit centre (x=300: floor 101, face 50). A currently runs 59–62 there.

Lay a 2-px near-black line (value ~28) across the full 464-px width at the top of that face band, so the wall band contains exactly one dominant horizontal edge instead of six equal-weight course joints at rows 53, 65, 69, 79, 93 and 107.

Insert a 4–6 px joint-free cap strip immediately above that shadow line, held at roughly floor value (~70), with no vertical joints crossing it — it is the arris, and it is the only element that tells the eye where the top plane ends.

Redraw the coursing above and below the arris at different scales: larger, low-contrast units above (stone tops seen in plan) and smaller, hard-jointed units below (stone faces in elevation). A's joint scale currently runs 18 px in the upper band and 8 px at the base, which is backwards and reinforces the single-plane read.

Darken the last 4 px of the face at the floor junction into a contact shadow. A does the opposite — at x=300 rows 113–116 climb to 82–85 against a 101 floor, so the wall brightens as it meets the ground.

Remove the per-course bevel: flatten each course so its top row and bottom row are within 1–2 values (currently 53→46 and 53→48), leaving only the recessed joint to describe the stone. That highlight survives the engine light being switched off.

S4.Q2:
B holds a top surface at a constant 90,90,90 from y=0 to y=29, ends it with a single 1-art-pixel arris at y=30–31 (147,143,134), then drops straight to a front face at 44,44,44 — the face sits at 49% of the top's value, a hard step with nothing between them. That face then has real extent: three block courses from y=32 to y=79, ~24 art px, with the middle course's vertical joints offset half a block from the courses above and below, so it reads as a masonry plane rather than a stripe. B also carries the read around the corner — the north-south wall at x=0–15 is the same 90 grey with block seams and *no* face at all, which is what that wall must look like from directly overhead, so the projection is consistent across both runs.
A never produces a top plane anywhere in frame: y=0 through y=116 is six repeats of one rhythm — dark line (9–30), bright line (36–109), body ramping downward (20→73) — and then a contact-shadow row at y=115–116 and floor. There is not one horizontal band in A free of course texture, so the wall is an elevation pasted above the floor with no measurable thickness, and it is also close to unreadable at played size: mean luminance across the wall band runs 15–70 of 255, and the posts and bottom rail only resolve when the image is brightened 2×.
flips: Cap A's wall. Cut the south-facing face on a straight vertical at the wall's end and expose 2–3 art px of core at a value between the new top and the face (top 90 / core ~65 / face 44 in B's terms), so the wall has a stated depth rather than an implied one — neither image does this now, and A, having no top at all, has nothing to state it against.
